title: Reducedness and rational-point density for a scheme product
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $X,Y$ be reduced finite-type $k$-schemes [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $A\subseteq X(k)$ and $B\subseteq Y(k)$ [def-weil-field-valued-points] have dense images in the underlying Zariski spaces $|X|$ and $|Y|$. Put $P=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}Y$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and let $C\subseteq P(k)$ consist of the paired rational points $(a,b):\operatorname{Spec}k\to P$ for $a\in A$ and $b\in B$, characterized by their two projections. Then $P$ is reduced, and the image of $C$ is dense in $|P|$. Empty schemes and empty dense subsets are allowed; $k$ need not be perfect and $X,Y$ need not be smooth or affine.

source.place: Section 1(a), Proposition 1.10 (printed pp.9-10), Proposition 1.11 and Remark 1.14 (printed p.10), applied successively to the two factors; Appendix A.43 (printed p.576), product reducedness; Section 1(c), proof of Theorem 1.45 (printed p.19).

proof.text: Choose affine open covers of $X$ and $Y$. For members $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}S$, the open subscheme $W=p^{-1}(U)\cap q^{-1}(V)$ of $P$ is $U\times_k V$: apply the open-preimage fibre-product statement twice and the defining universal property. The affine-product statement identifies $W$ with $\operatorname{Spec}T$, $T=R\otimes_k S$, with its two specified projections. These $W$ cover $P$. Write $A_U$ and $B_V$ for the rational points in $A$ and $B$ whose images lie in $U$ and $V$. Their images are dense in $U$ and $V$, since every nonempty open in either affine open is also open in the original scheme. The pairs from $A_U\times B_V$ lie in $W$ by their projections.

source.place: Proposition 1.10, proof (b) implies (c), affine localization; Appendix A.43, reduction to affine products. Stacks Tags 01JR and 01I4.

proof.text: For $a\in A_U$, let $e_a:R\to k$ be the $k$-algebra homomorphism corresponding to $a$ by the affine-spectrum statement; similarly put $e_b:S\to k$ for $b\in B_V$. These families detect zero. Indeed, if $e_a(r)=0$ for every $a\in A_U$, the closed set $V((r))$ contains the dense image of $A_U$, hence is all of $\operatorname{Spec}R$. The radical/intersection statement for the zero ideal gives $r\in\sqrt{(0)}$, so $r$ is nilpotent. The reducedness definition makes $R=\mathcal O_X(U)$ reduced, hence $r=0$. The identical argument with $S,B_V$ proves its zero-detection assertion.

source.place: Proposition 1.10, proof (b) implies (c), printed p.10; use all prime ideals for the full scheme topology (Stacks Tag 00E0(7)).

proof.text: For every pair $(a,b)\in A_U\times B_V$, the algebra tensor-product universal property gives $E_{a,b}:T\to k$, $E_{a,b}(r\otimes s)=e_a(r)e_b(s)$. The affine-product projection formulas and uniqueness of the paired point identify $\operatorname{Spec}E_{a,b}$ with $(a,b)$. We show that the $E_{a,b}$ detect zero. Suppose $E_{a,b}(t)=0$ for all pairs. For fixed $a$, form the linear contraction $L_a:T\to S$, $r\otimes s\mapsto e_a(r)s$. On every pure tensor $e_b L_a=E_{a,b}$, so these maps agree everywhere since pure tensors generate. Step 2 gives $L_a(t)=0$. The canonical map $\mu:k\otimes_k S\to S$, $c\otimes s\mapsto cs$, has inverse $s\mapsto1\otimes s$: the two inverse equations follow from $c\otimes s=1\otimes cs$ and generation by pure tensors. Thus $L_a=\mu\circ(e_a\otimes\mathrm{id}_S)$ implies $(e_a\otimes\mathrm{id}_S)(t)=0$ for all $a$. Apply the cited tensor-family zero-detection lemma with $M=R$, $N=S$, $J=A_U$, $P_a=k$, and $f_a=e_a$, whose hypothesis was verified in step 2. It gives $t=0$.

source.place: Proposition 1.11 and Remark 1.14, printed p.10, with the family-injectivity argument supplied by the cited tensor lemma and successive evaluations in the two factors.

proof.text: If $t\in T$ is nilpotent, then $E_{a,b}(t)$ is nilpotent in the field $k$ for every pair, hence zero: for $z\ne0$ an equation $z^n=0$ contradicts multiplication by $(z^{-1})^n$. Step 3 gives $t=0$. Thus $T$ is reduced, and the affine-scheme reducedness equivalence makes $W=\operatorname{Spec}T$ reduced. Applying reducedness on the open cover of step 1 shows that $P$ is reduced.

source.place: Proposition 1.10 (c) implies (b), and Appendix A.43; Stacks Tags 01J2 and 01J1.

proof.text: The paired points are dense in each $W=\operatorname{Spec}T$. To see this, let $F\subseteq W$ be a closed subset containing their images. In the Zariski topology $F=V(I)$ for an ideal $I\subseteq T$. For $t\in I$ and every pair, membership $\ker E_{a,b}\in V(I)$ says $E_{a,b}(t)=0$. Step 3 implies $t=0$, so $I=(0)$ and $F=W$. The closure in $P$ of the image of $C$ therefore contains every $W$ of step 1: its intersection with $W$ is closed in $W$ and contains all these local pairs. As those $W$ cover $P$, that closure is $P$. This proves the required density. If a factor is empty, the product is empty and reduced, with empty dense image. The same argument already allows empty $A_U$ or $B_V$: step 2 then forces the corresponding coordinate ring to be zero, and step 3 uses a lemma that explicitly allows an empty index set.

source.place: Proposition 1.10, affine evaluation criterion, applied to paired points; Proposition 1.11 and Remark 1.14, successive evaluation. Zariski closed sets as in Stacks Tag 00E0.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 1.10, Proposition 1.11 and Remark 1.14, printed pp.9–10; affine-local double-evaluation argument, with tensor-family injectivity supplied by the existing Lean-closed node. Compare Appendix A.43, printed p.576.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q10-8cea933be (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery and the source: Milne AG2017 Def 1.9, Props 1.10/1.11 and Rem 1.14 (pp.9-10), A.43 (p.576). There are no new nodes, and compared with clones/live the item's statement, source, stmt_deps and blueprint are unchanged. The statement is true. It fails to apply only when no dense set of rational points exists, e.g. k=F_p(t), x^p=t has no k-points. The empty cases hold. Steps 1-5 check against the cited statements. (1) Opens W=p^-1U∩q^-1V are Spec(R⊗S) by the open-preimage node used twice and the affine-spectra node. (2) Dense-evaluation zero detection holds by the radical clause √0=∩p plus reducedness. (3) E_{a,b} comes from the algebra-tensor universal property. The contraction plus the same-unit node lem-sfb-vector-space-tensor-family-zero-detection gives t=0; that node allows an empty J and its hypothesis is exactly step 2. (4) T is reduced, then P is reduced by the affine-reduced node and the open-cover node. (5) A closed V(I) containing every ker E forces I=0, so the pairs are dense; this is a separate argument from step 4. Batch-5 flag: lem-trf-reduced-scheme-open-cover is a Mathlib leaf (IsReduced.iff_of_openCover, Properties.lean:140), a general fact about schemes. Neither the trace-formula nor the Poincaré-duality assumption gives it, and it is not a step of their proofs, so I accept the citation. FIX: step 3 uses the uniqueness of the paired point (a,b) from the fibre-product universal property but did not cite def-pc-fibre-product; I added it to step 3's uses (C1/C4).
